dossier.public_summary: The dip is seen at very different depths in different sectors and even in the same instrument, and the four individual dips do not agree, so the signal is not stable. A second dip near the opposite phase and a low planet-like score point to a blended binary rather than a planet on the target M dwarf.

reasons.why: depth really changes between sectors (chi2=13.05 dof=2 depth_change_pct=137.6), as confirmed by sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source (p_constant=0.000575992).
individual transits are inconsistent (chi2=21.778027881576993 dof=3) with sector depths 7196, 1140, 9164 ppm; top 3 carry 0.999 of signal so not spokojny pulsations.
secondary at phase 0.7923 near the complementary phase (offset 0.2923) with dip-like amplitude 11.6% of primary favours blended eclipsing binary with phase shift, not a planet.
independent scorer ranks much below median planet (0.5) and below 0.1 false-positive regime threshold, consistent with variability/binary explanation.
